expected.summary: Fourteen minutes before the anchor the ML platform team published a new ranking model, reco-two-tower-v19 (ML-1043), and recommendation hot-loaded it from the model registry, one pod every forty five seconds, with no release and no version change. The new model is 2.1 GiB against 0.6 GiB for reco-two-tower-v18, and for requests without precomputed recommendations (cache.hit false, about 30 percent) inference on a loaded pod now takes about 640 ms, so recommendation's own spans slowed sharply while reco-db stays flat and recommendation returns no errors. web-bff and mobile-bff call reco.for_user with a 500 ms timeout and treat it as optional, so the timeout does not fail the page, but the 500 ms wait alone pushes their /home handling past edge-gateway's own 500 ms timeout on the BFFs. About a third of GET /home requests now fail with 504 timeout after 500ms calling web-bff or mobile-bff, and the 504s propagate to edge-gateway, where the alert fires; every other route is healthy. The BFFs' degraded render warnings, saying /home was served without personalised rows, are a symptom of the timeouts, and the BFFs, catalog and auth did not change.
contributingFactors: reco-two-tower-v19 hot-loaded by recommendation with no release, raising inference time past 500 ms for requests without precomputed recommendations
the BFFs' 500 ms timeout on the optional recommendation call matching edge-gateway's 500 ms timeout on the BFFs, so an optional call can still fail the page

criteria.description: Does the brief name recommendation hot-loading the larger reco-two-tower-v19 model (ML-1043) as the origin, with inference on cache misses slowing past the BFFs' 500 ms timeout, and explain that although the call is optional the wait takes /home past edge-gateway's timeout on the BFFs? 5 = the model swap, the slow inference, the optional call whose timeout still fails the page and the victim chain. Blaming the BFFs, catalog or reco-db scores at most 2.

Is it grounded in recommendation's server spans slowing while reco-db stays flat and recommendation returns no errors, the reco.for_user client timeouts on the BFFs, the GET /home 504s at edge-gateway, and the model registry load logs lining up pod by pod? Cap at 3 unless it explains why an optional call fails the page.
Does it avoid blaming web-bff, mobile-bff, catalog, auth, reco-db or a deploy, and treat the degraded render warnings as a symptom?
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
